case: ODUMA campaign: six LAS files generated by w5c/welldata/gen_case.mjs into src/content/capstone-cases/welldata, downloaded from the capstone card

beginner.d5: welldata beginner holds capstone attempts in production (the W1 attempts listing: about 7 to 10). This file re-keys it, so it carries the D5 allowlist mechanism with the allowlist EMPTY: it refuses until the owner signs the attempt ids off (apply.sh attempts lists them) and the lead regenerates it with ALLOW.
beginner.dataset: ODUMA capstone case: six LAS files (oduma1_wrapped, oduma2_main, oduma3_feet, oduma4_irregular, oduma5_nulls, oduma6_spliced), downloaded from the capstone card
beginner.prompt: The ODUMA campaign: six LAS files delivered from the ODUMA field. Download them from the capstone case files on this card, open each one in the LAS inspector with Open your own LAS files, and read its QC panel. Report the requested values exactly as the parser shows them: sample and null counts are integers. Report (1) the depth samples in oduma2_main; (2) its GR null samples; (3) its mean GR over finite samples; (4) the oduma3_feet depth step converted to metres; (5) the PEF null samples in oduma5_nulls; and (6) the depth samples in oduma1_wrapped.
beginner.why: Section 3 pick A: every graded value was printed by the beginner walkthrough and the LAS inspector opened on basic_20. The capstone moves to the ODUMA case, which no panel preloads; the learner downloads the files and opens them in the inspector.

oduma2_n_samples.prompt_precision: Report the requested values exactly as the parser shows them: sample and null counts are integers
oduma2_n_samples.evidence: Samples / NULL tile prints qc.depth.nSamples for oduma2_main once opened: 437. lasio 0.32 reads the same count (w5c/welldata/oracle_lasio.py). Integer count at tol 0.

oduma2_gr_nulls.prompt_precision: Report the requested values exactly as the parser shows them: sample and null counts are integers
oduma2_gr_nulls.evidence: GR row nulls column prints c.nullCount = 13; RHOB beside it carries 5. lasio agrees.

oduma2_gr_mean.evidence: num(v, 4) prints 76.9970 against 76.99698143635156; tol 0.05 is far wider than half a unit of the 4th decimal. lasio's float32 nanmean is identical.

oduma3_step_m.evidence: Step tile prints the average native step 0.2500 F and 0.0762 m (0.25 x 0.3048); graded 0.0762 tol 0.001. The float32 first difference 0.07617 also passes; the 0.3048 factor unapplied (0.25) fails.

oduma5_pef_nulls.prompt_precision: Report the requested values exactly as the parser shows them: sample and null counts are integers
oduma5_pef_nulls.evidence: oduma5_nulls PEF row (dead, red) prints nulls 241; the file flags nulls with -9999, which the parser reads from ~Well NULL. NPHI is also dead with the same count, so the field checks the dead-curve reading.

oduma1_n_samples.prompt_precision: Report the requested values exactly as the parser shows them: sample and null counts are integers
oduma1_n_samples.evidence: oduma1_wrapped (LAS 1.2, WRAP YES) Samples tile prints 207; the data section has four physical lines per sample, the taught trap.

intermediate.dataset: ODUMA capstone case: oduma3_feet and oduma4_irregular, downloaded from the capstone card
intermediate.prompt: Run the full import pipeline on oduma3_feet.las from the ODUMA capstone case files (download them from this card and open them in the import explorer with Open your own LAS files) and read the import panel: the start depth, the stop depth and the depth step converted to metres, how many curves needed unit conversion, and how many curve kinds the importer recognised. Then report the number of depth samples in oduma4_irregular.las, the case file whose depth step changes size down the log.
intermediate.why: Section 3 pick A: every graded value was printed by the intermediate walkthrough and the import panel opened on feet_20. The capstone moves to the ODUMA case, which no panel preloads.

oduma3_start_md_m.evidence: fmt(prep.startMdM, 8) prints 2139.69604492 m; tol 0.01 also passes the hand answer 7020 x 0.3048 = 2139.696.

oduma3_stop_md_m.evidence: fmt(prep.stopMdM, 8) prints 2169.26171875 m; tol 0.01 also passes 7117 x 0.3048 = 2169.2616.

oduma3_import_step_m.evidence: fmt(r.step, 12) prints 0.076171875000 m exactly (the float32 first difference); tol 0.001 also passes 0.0762.

oduma3_converted_curves.evidence: prints 3: DEPT (F), DT (US/F) and TVD (F) are flagged YES in the table. A metre-only reader who counts the sonic alone gives 2.

oduma3_recognized_kinds.evidence: prints 6: GR, RHOB, NPHI, DT, ILD and SP recognised; TVD and TENS read 'not recognised'. Eight curves after the index, so a curve count gives 8.

oduma4_n_samples.evidence: with oduma4_irregular open the Samples tile prints 173 rows; the uniform-step tile prints 0 beside it. lasio agrees.

advanced.dataset: ODUMA capstone case: all six LAS files, downloaded from the capstone card
advanced.prompt: Run the full import pipeline on all six ODUMA capstone case files as one campaign (download them from this card and open them together in the campaign explorer with Open your own LAS files as a campaign) and read the campaign panel: total curves imported (depth excluded), files needing depth unit conversion, dead curves detected, files with a uniform depth step, depth samples parsed from the wrapped LAS 1.2 file oduma1_wrapped, and total flagged nulls in oduma5_nulls.
advanced.why: Section 3 pick A: every graded value was printed by the advanced walkthrough and the campaign panel opened on the teaching campaign. The capstone moves to the ODUMA campaign, which no panel preloads.

oduma_campaign_curves.evidence: prints 31 for the six ODUMA files (5+8+4+5+5+4, depth excluded). lasio agrees.

oduma_converted_files.evidence: prints 3: oduma1_wrapped, oduma3_feet and oduma6_spliced log depth in feet; no metre file carries a feet-referenced curve, so the tile counts depth conversions only.

oduma_dead_curves.evidence: prints 2: NPHI and PEF in oduma5_nulls. A file count gives 1.

oduma_uniform_files.evidence: prints 4 of 6: oduma4_irregular and oduma6_spliced (two runs at 0.5 and 0.25 ft) fail. Counting the failures gives 2.

oduma1_wrapped_samples.evidence: the per-file table prints samples 207 for oduma1_wrapped; the data section holds four times as many physical lines.

oduma5_flagged_nulls.evidence: prints 525 = GR 37 + RHOB 6 + NPHI 241 + PEF 241 in the per-curve composition. lasio agrees.
